main_text.head: SECT. I.
main_text.p: DE Juramenti Caufis Materiali & Efficiente, in superioribus actum eft: de Causa Formali nunc agendum. Cum autem duplex fit rei alicujus Forma: Externa, & Interna: quæ hujus sunt [?]lassis, ad duo capita ita revocanda sunt, ut quæ ad Juramenti verba aut signa pertinent, eò quòd sensibus exterioribus [?]ercipiantur, Externa Forma nomine [?]eniant; quæ vero ad ejusdem sensum & interpretationem, quod interioris [?]nentis est opus, Forma Interna. Re-pectu Externæ Formæ, Juramentum ut signis solùm constat, aut verbis solùm, aut utrisque. Dubium itaque pri-Casus 32num est de eo Juramento, quod signo solùm fit sine verbis. Fuerunt qui existi-narent, nisi expresse adhibito aut verbo Juro, aut Dei nomine, dicendo Juro me facturum, vel per Deum faciam, Deum estor, Ita me Deus adjuvet, vel quid simile; nudam esse promissionem, non tem Juramentum: & proinde obligare quidem sub poena mendacii, sed non sub poena perjurii; ita ut qui non fecerit quod pollicitus est, reus fit violatæ fidei

page.notes: The left edge of the scan cuts off the first letters of several lines (e.g. "lassis", "ercipiantur", "eniant", "nentis"); these are marked [?] and reconstructed from context. "Juro" in the italic phrase is partly cropped at the left edge and read from context. The sidenote is printed "Cafus", transcribed as Casus. Small marks (a star beside "exterioribus", a dot near the sidenote) are not printed text and are omitted. The word "Cum'autem" has a small mark that is treated as a space. The final word of the column, "quæ", is the catchword; the text ends at "violatæ fidei". Printed text on the page is otherwise read with confidence.
